title: Why a 1 TB drive shows less

yt.title: A 1 TB drive shows {c_gib} GB. Where did the rest go? #Shorts
yt.description:
1 TB = 10^12 bytes. Operating systems often report in gibibytes (2^30 bytes): 10^12 / 2^30 = {c_gib}. The bytes did not go anywhere; the unit changed.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: A 1 TB drive is not 1 TB
scenes.narration: You buy a one terabyte drive, plug it in, and your computer shows less. Where did the rest go?

scenes.label: what many systems show for 1 terabyte
scenes.narration: A terabyte is one trillion bytes. Many systems count in units of two to the thirty bytes, and label them G B. One trillion divided by that is about {c_gib_say}.
Nothing is missing. Drive makers use powers of ten. Operating systems often use powers of two. Same bytes, different unit.
